what: The registered report's confirmatory tests are recorded: hypothesis without lab_event, test.registration = B1 (the OSF registration's DOI), anchor `registry`. Neither the paper nor anything this conversion could read gives the registration's date (the OSF API refuses automated reads), so `planned_at` is left out, as rule 43 allows for a registered test (warning 36 asks for it). In the first 0.39 attempt, before rule 43 was revised, the tests had to be removed.
need: registered tests whose registration date is not at hand
proposal: core: rule 43 revised (planned_at optional with anchor registry)
v0.39: resolved: rule 43 revised; the tests are recorded without the date

what: The test structure is built for lab records. An external registered report fits only by leaving `hypothesis.lab_event` and `lab_plan` out; `planned_at` cannot be given an anchor (no `registry` value), and the Stage 1 in-principle acceptance has no field.
need: external registration as an anchor; registered-report stage
v0.39: resolved in form (anchor `registry`, test.registration as a reference); the in-principle acceptance stage is for the preregistration extension; blocked here by planned_at (new entry)

what: The source's decision rule is interpretive (Jeffreys' scale, 'ambiguous'), not a stated threshold; I wrote rules at BF 3 and 1/3 that the source does not state. A converted claim's `test` can only be as precise as the paper, and there is no way to mark rules as the converter's reading.
need: provenance of a reconstructed decision rule
v0.39: resolved: field_provenance marks reconstructed rules `inferred` (spec §3.3.3 guidance); the rules no longer invent thresholds, citing Jeffreys' scale as the paper does

what: Recruitment pool, response rate (6%), compensation (none), manipulation checks and the 68% exclusion are central to a behavioural experiment and are text only.
The measure (single item) and the construct (trust) are separate definitions, but nothing links D6 to D9: the format cannot say D6 measures D9.
Inclusion Bayes factors per effect fit `conditions: {effect: …}`; the effect being a definition or an interaction of two is free text.
The deviation from the registered plan is a limitation with category `other`: there is no `deviation` category outside lab records.
